benchmark.title: Benchmark
benchmark.subtitle: Compare your pace with recreational swimmers in your age group
benchmark.methodology: Benchmarks reflect recreational 25m pool fitness swimmers (Apple Fitness style), not competitive long-course times. Pace slows slightly with age; women typically ~12–18s slower per 100m than men in the same bracket.
benchmark.profileRequired: Set your sex and age in Settings to see benchmarks.

feedback.firstSession: Great start! Your first swim is logged — every champion began with a single lap.

feedback.motivationGoal: You hit your distance goal. That is something to be proud of — trust the process.

feedback.motivationConsistent2: You are building a real rhythm in the pool — consistency is your superpower.
feedback.motivationKeepGoing: Another session in the books. Keep stacking these workouts and the numbers will follow.
feedback.motivationKeepGoing2: Logged and done — every lap you swim is building something bigger.
feedback.motivationKeepGoing3: One more session banked. Stay patient and the pace will come.

feedback.coachMonthDown: This month has been lighter so far. One steady week can turn that around.
feedback.motivationTrendUp: Your recent pace trend is moving the right way — keep trusting the work.
feedback.tipFirst: Log a few more sessions and the app can compare trends, benchmarks, and habits for you.
feedback.tipConsistency: It has been {days} days since your last swim. A short session still keeps the habit alive.
feedback.tipRecovery: Pace and heart rate both suggest a harder day. An easier next swim can help you absorb the work.
feedback.tipDeveloping: Focus on smooth breathing and steady laps — consistency will pull pace down over time.
feedback.tipStrokeVariety: {stroke} was {percent}% of today's swim. Mixing strokes can balance muscles and keep training fresh.

feedback.tipImprovingTrend: Your pace trend is improving — this is a good moment to keep the rhythm steady rather than forcing more.
feedback.tipNearGoal: You were {meters} m shy of your distance goal — close enough that the next swim could nail it.
feedback.tipDefault: Keep stacking sessions like this. Regular laps beat one perfect workout every time.
feedback.tipDefault2: Trust the routine — steady sessions like this add up faster than you think.
feedback.tipDefault3: Small, consistent swims win over time. This session is another brick in the wall.
